english.title: Parent permit excluded pupil to be present in a public place during school hours on a school day
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the parent of a pupil, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NAME..), of compulsory school age who was

(A)_[excluded for a fixed period of **(..SPECIFY THE PERIOD..)]_
(B)_[permanently excluded]_

on disciplinary grounds from a relevant school in England, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SCHOOL..), and having been given a notice under section 104 of the Education and Inspection Act 2006, failed to ensure that

(C)_[he]_
(D)_[she]_

was not present in a public place at any time during school hours

(E)_[on a day which was one of the first five school days to which the exclusion related]_
(F)_[on any of the days to which that exclusion related]_

and was stated in that notice
english.legislation: Contrary to section 103 of the Education and Inspections Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

failed to ensure that he/she was not present in a public place
at any time during school hours on a day
which is one of the first five school days to which the exclusion relates OR

english.notes:
(i) Subsection 103(4) of the Education and Inspection Act 2006 provides a defence where a person charged with an offence under subsection 103(3) of the Act if he/she can prove that they had a reasonable justification for their failure to comply with the duty imposed by subsection (2).
(ii) Subsection 103(6) of the Education and Inspection Act 2006 provides that proceedings for an offence under subsection 103(3) of the Act may not be instituted except by a local education authority.
(iii) Subsection 103(7) of the Education and Inspection Act 2006 provides that where the excluded pupil is excluded during the course of a school day but before the beginning of any afternoon session on that day, that day is to be treated for the purposes of subsection 103(2)(a) of the Act as the first day to which the exclusion relates.
